# `scripts/post-process/parquet_vs_fits_test.py`

Source: [parquet_vs_fits_test.py](../../../../scripts/post-process/parquet_vs_fits_test.py)

Test: the pipeline's FITS halo tables (compress\_halo\_outputs.py, .fits.gz) rewritten as Parquet. For each file:
sizes, write time, read times (whole table, two columns, a mass cut), and a bit-exact round trip of every column.

usage: parquet\_vs\_fits\_test.py &lt;out\_dir&gt; &lt;file.fits.gz&gt; [...]
Parquet variants (pyarrow): zstd level 3; zstd 3 + BYTE\_STREAM\_SPLIT for float columns; zstd 9 + split; gzip 6
(the same codec as .fits.gz). Row groups of 1M rows. Header cards and the PROVENANCE HDU go into the schema metadata
(key 'fits\_header\_&lt;hdu&gt;' = JSON of the cards, 'provenance' = JSON of the PROVENANCE table), so nothing is lost.
Timings: wall clock, best of 3, files read from the file system just written to (page cache warm for both).

## Contents

- [`best`](#best) - Best (minimum) wall time of `n` calls of `f` and the last result.
- [`header_json`](#header_json) - FITS header records as a JSON list of [name, value, comment] (for the Parquet metadata).
- [`main`](#main) - Command line: `parquet_vs_fits_test.py <out dir> <file.fits.gz>...`: size, write and read times of FITS against Parquet per file, with a round-trip check.
